title: slicer land checks a merged branch and marks its slice done
lead: `slicer land ID --branch BRANCH --note TEXT` checks that the branch is merged into HEAD and that the slice's relay runs have ended, then runs `done --render --check`, and prints the git commands left for the person landing (commit, worktree remove, branch delete). slicer itself still commits nothing.
findings_note: outer-session wishlist 2026-10-16, item 6: landing is about seven hand-run steps per slice
boundary: **Not in this slice:** running the suite; merging; running the printed git commands; slivers (`done` with several ids keeps that path).

sections.heading: Why
Files
Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests with fixture repos that are their own git repos, and watch them go red.
2. Add the checks and reuse `done`; then the CLI and the printed commands.
3. Docs and CHANGELOG; mutation-check (skip the ancestor check; skip the run check).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
